_comment: The contract between this harness and everything that reads its output.
Consumers: effpretty (renders the console stream), efftriage (diagnoses failures from the
structured stream), effverify (grades runs), and mission-control (dispatch, history, impact).
None of them are in this repository, and none of them can fail this repository's CI --- so a
rewording here is invisible until someone notices their tooling has quietly stopped working.
That is not hypothetical. On 2026-08-21 a refactor reworded eight of efftriage's thirteen
matchers at once and nothing failed: tests green, runs green, triage silently explaining
nothing. One rule had already died the same way on 2026-08-13.

So this file is the contract. Nothing in THIS repository asserts the code still matches it --- the contract tests live in testops-tools (tae-conversion/tests/harness_contract_tests.py) and only run when somebody runs that
suite, so a break lands green here and goes red later. Moving them in needs a gradle config change. Until then: if you change the harness's output, change this file in
the same commit and tell the consumers.

console._comment: The human stream, on logcat tag 'Eff'. effpretty parses `^(\s*)\[([A-Z]+)\](.*)$`, so the tag, the glyph and four-space-per-level indentation are all load-bearing.

structured._comment: The machine stream, one JSON object per line on logcat tag 'EffJson'. Demuxed by `effpretty --events` into run-events.jsonl.

event_envelope._comment: Every record carries one eventEnvelope object containing these fields. Existing top-level type, ts, testId, and payload fields remain for version-1 consumers; eventType and wallTimeMs are their typed envelope equivalents. unassigned/fallback is explicit compatibility evidence, not a generated run identity.

structured._state_comment: state: compatibility projection of the typed stateSnapshot, written by StateProbe. `phase` is arrival|afterSetup|start|end|afterCleanup. Arrival is outside every cleanup rule; afterSetup is the enforced app/runtime isolation boundary before Activity launch; start is after Activity setup; end is after the test body; afterCleanup is the verified handoff when the process survives. Consumers pair them by testId and compute transitions. The remaining keys are counts (tabs, tabsPrivate, pendingUndoTabs, recentlyClosedStoreTabs, history, bookmarks, logins, addresses, creditCards, sitePermissions, savedSessions, collections, tabGroups, tabGroupAssignments, recentlyClosedTabs, topSites, downloads, preferenceOverrideCount), allowlisted preference identity (preferenceOverrideIds), execution identity/runtime state (processId, searchActive, voiceInputRequested, voiceInputResult), and launcherIcon. A string beginning 'unreadable:' is a failed observation and makes an enforced isolation boundary unverifiable.
structured._state_snapshot_comment: stateSnapshot: the versioned capture-only state contract. Each contributor declares a stable name, schemaVersion, captureCost, sensitivity, completeness, compatibility projection, legacy boundaryPolicy, resourcePolicy (OBSERVE, RESTORE, PRESERVE, or UNSUPPORTED), boundaryBaseline, controlDrivers, and values. Capture never restores or mutates state. The flat state record remains during consumer migration and contains only contributors whose values preserve its existing baseline semantics.
structured._cleanup_comment: cleanup: emitted by AppDataCleaner once per phase. `phase` is before|after, `failed` is a comma-separated list of the clears that errored, and `failureDetails` maps those stable step names to exception type and message. A failed clear and a genuine state leak otherwise look identical --- both present as a later test starting with state it did not create --- so this is what distinguishes them.
structured._attempt_end_comment: attemptEnd is the only atomic terminal record. It is emitted by the outermost BaseTest rule after the body, efficiency cleanup, isolation verification, and environment restoration return or throw. testEnd remains the compatibility body-result event and is not evidence that cleanup completed. A host collector synthesizes an incomplete or crash outcome when this record is absent.
structured._environment_comment: environmentPreflight and environmentRestore record the declared device, permission, notification, shared-artifact, and mock-server requirements together with allowlisted observations from both sides of the operation. activityEnvironment records orientation application after the Activity exists, because pre-launch target Resources can be stale.
structured._activity_lifecycle_comment: activityLifecycle: a monotonic per-test trace from Application.ActivityLifecycleCallbacks. created records whether Android supplied saved instance state; every activity record carries process, activity-instance, task, intent-flag, lifecycle, and process-global search/voice state. This distinguishes an expected same-task restore from a fresh task inheriting stale process state.
structured._scope_type_comment: Step records use scopeType for STEP/CMD/LOC. The top-level type remains the domain record identity stepEnd; using type for both fields caused the scope to overwrite the record identity before version 3.

failure_vocabulary._comment: core/VerbHost.kt, object Failure. Triage rules match these VALUES rather than the prose beside them, which is the entire point: a value cannot be reworded by accident.

optional_fields._comment: Not on every record, but consumers rely on them where present.
optional_fields.verb: the verb that produced the record, e.g. click, verify, navigate
optional_fields.backend: UI tree used for the observation
optional_fields.tree: merged or unmerged Compose semantics tree, when applicable
optional_fields.semanticRoles: readiness roles the selector contributes to
optional_fields.value: what the selector searched for --- efftriage T20 matches this against dump nodes
optional_fields.expectation: what was asked of the element, e.g. 'is selected'
optional_fields.dump: label of the screen dump taken for this failure, pairing it with the dumpNode records
optional_fields.page: page name, on navigate and arrival records
optional_fields.attempts: number of fresh observations made by the verb
optional_fields.actionAttempts: number of bounded actions performed by a driveUntil-style verb
optional_fields.timedOut: whether the expected condition missed its deadline
optional_fields.lastObservation: typed summary of the final fresh observation
optional_fields.failureCategory: assertion, harness, infrastructure, timeout, or inapplicable
optional_fields.screen: page tracked when the verb ran
optional_fields.navigationEdge: route executing when the verb ran, when applicable

screen_dump._comment: helpers/ScreenDump.kt. efftriage greps the markers; the structured dumpNode records carry the same nodes as fields.
